text:
jerry: quick follow-up from the afternoon design review: i'm proposing we trial a "compat-probe" handshake for Private runtimes so Hosted routing can do safe fallbacks without requiring full policy translation. thoughts?

nina: high level ok - what does the handshake return? capability-set, stability score, and an auth hint?

jerry: yep. minimal example:
```
{
  "capabilities": ["streaming", "kv-cache", "quant-8bit"],
  "stability": "beta",   // stable | beta | experimental
  "hint": "signed-manifest-v1"  // how to bind or authenticate
}
```

oliver: named hints are nice. prefer a signed short-lived capability_token instead of hints so Hosted doesn't need to fetch manifests at request time. token contains capability IDs and expiry.

kevin: token approach ok but ops concern: who mints tokens in Private? customer controlplane or our controlplane acting as broker? both have different trust models.

jerry: plan A: Private controlplane mints tokens; Plan B: Private publishes signed manifests that Hosted can validate with tenant-bound keys (preferred for air-gapped customers).

nina: also need to define usage: are tokens consulted per-request or only during route resolution? per-request expensive; prefer route-resolve time with a cached route binding and TTL.

oliver: agree. route-binding TTL should be conservative (e.g., 60s) and we need fast invalidation path for revokes.

kevin: revocation is hard if tokens live outside our controlplane. require a revocation-list pull endpoint on Private runtimes OR include a revocation_nonce in route-bind metadata that we can bump.

infra-bot: note: any mechanism that requires Hosted to fetch from Private at runtime will raise firewall/egress issues for some customers. prefer push/persist model.

jerry: right, that's why signed-manifests + tenant keys looks promising. flow sketch:
1) Private runtime signs a manifest (capabilities + expiry + revocation_nonce) with tenant key
2) controlplane pulls manifest at bind-time (or customer uploads it) and validates signature
3) controlplane issues a short binding to Hosted (opaque binding ID) which references the manifest; Hosted uses binding ID to route - no live fetch to Private

nina: good. that keeps runtime-talk out of request path. also adds audit trail in controlplane.

kevin: legal check: if manifest includes any PII-like metadata about endpoints, we need to scrub or encrypt. legal-bot: flagged for review.

legal-bot: reminder: any tenant-supplied manifests must be treated as customer data. record consent at onboarding and ensure manifests stored in encrypted blobstore with restricted access. also document retention TTL.

oliver: implementation question: how do we handle capability upgrades? e.g., Private adds streaming mid-binding. do we auto-refresh binding or require explicit rebind?

jerry: proposal: auto-refresh on expiry or when tenant triggers rebind. controlplane emits a "binding-updated" event and notifies route owners. auto-apply only for non-security-affecting capabilities (eg streaming), require opt-in for kms/auth changes.

nina: telemetry: emit metrics for binding-age, refresh-rate, and binding-failures. also surface reason codes for fallback (capability-mismatch vs capacity vs auth).

kevin: testing: synthetic scenario where Hosted falls back to a compatible model variant when binding lacks streaming. simulate cold-binding path and measure added p50/p95. oliver: add harness for that.

infra-bot: ops checklist suggestion: key enrollment docs, manifest format spec, revocation procedure, firewall guidance, and a canary tenant list for rollout.

jerry: rollout plan: 1) dry-run mode where we record what would have happened (no routing changes) 2) tenant opt-in via console/CLI 3) limited canary (10 tenants) 4) broader roll. include kill-switch feature-flag at org-level.

legal-bot: also ensure we have SLA language for Private-hosted fallbacks. customers may expect consistent behavior; call out fallback semantics clearly.

nina: UX: console should show binding health and last-probe time. also show "why a request routed to hosted" with reason code and link to remediation.

oliver: final note on security: require manifests to include a key_id and pointer to tenant key rotation policy. controlplane should validate that key is enrolled and not expired.

jerry: great feedback. i'll draft the spec with: manifest v1 schema, binding lifecycle, TTLs, revocation flow, telemetry events, ops checklist, and legal checklist. will post PR link. tagging @nina @kevin for review when ready. :rocket:

kevin: thanks, ping me for ops signoff once runbook is ready

nina: will review schema and telemetry bits

oliver: i'll mock the harness tests and measure latency impact

infra-bot: created follow-up ticket INFRA-3121 for firewall/docs work

jerry: closing thread, will share draft later today.
